Nice — keep it simple. A few quick rules of thumb:

- Delete obvious junk: promos, marketing, social pings, and things you never open. If you haven’t opened that sender in 2–3 months, delete.
- Delete trivially replaceable notifications: one-line alerts or duplicates that add no lasting value.
- Keep financial/legal/ tax records until you’ve reconciled them or until any required retention period has passed.
- Archive (tuck away) reference material you might need later: receipts you’ll need for returns, project notes, travel confirmations, and meaningful personal messages.
- Archive ongoing threads or anything awaiting follow-up; mark unread or snooze so it resurfaces when needed.
- Use a short “maybe” rule: if you’re unsure, archive now and delete if you haven’t needed it in 6 months.
- Unsubscribe aggressively — reducing incoming clutter makes future decisions easier.
- Prefer delete when an item is (1) replaceable, (2) not actionable, and (3) unlikely to be useful; prefer archive when it’s non-actionable but potentially useful later.

Would you like me to help apply these rules to your inbox? If so, I’ll first list the exact actions I would take (which messages/threads, how many, scope) and ask for your explicit confirmation before doing anything.
